value.rationale: The bias calibration problem is natural because small integer states experience rare successful stochastic-rounding progress. Under a fixed aggregate total-variation budget, uniform or naive bias has an order-M log M expected time, whereas the exactly optimal policy halves the leading coefficient and changes fluctuation scale and limiting family. Provides a precise finite-state numerical design benchmark with sharp asymptotics; not merely a known coupon identity or a routine narrow numeric recomputation.
